source_text:
17.9 ̓Ανέβη καπνὸς ἐν ὀργῇ αὐτοῦ,
καὶ πῦρ ἀπὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ κατεφλόγισεν, α νθρακες ἀνήφθησαν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ.
̓Ωργίσθη, φησὶ, καὶ κατέβαλεν τὸ πῦρ, δι' ου πάλιν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους κατέφλεγεν.
Ανθρακες, ὁ τῶν ἀποστόλων χορός· τούτου γὰρ τοῦ πυρὸς κατὰ τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς Πεν
τηκοστῆς μεταλαβόντες, καὶ γλώσσας ἐπὶ τῶν κεφαλῶν πυρίνας δεξάμενοι,
α νθρακες εἰκότως ἐχρημάτιζον, φωτίζοντες ὁμοῦ τὰ ε θνη καὶ καθάροντες· ο τι
ταῦτα ἐγένετο, τοῖς ἑξῆς ἐπαγομένοις μάνθανε·
pass_a_gloss: Went-up smoke in anger of-him, and fire from face of-him set-ablaze, coals were-kindled from him. He-was-angered, he-says, and he-cast-down the fire, through which again the men he-was-burning. Coals, the of-the apostles chorus; of-this for of-the fire according-to the day of-the Pentecost having-partaken, and tongues upon the heads fiery having-received, coals reasonably they-were-called, lighting together the nations and purifying; that these happened, to-the next being-brought learn:
pass_b_english: “Smoke went up in his anger, and fire from his face set ablaze, coals were kindled from him” (Psalm 17:9).

He was angry, he says, and he cast down the fire, through which again he burned the men. Coals: the chorus of the apostles; for having partaken of this fire on the day of Pentecost, and having received fiery tongues upon their heads, they were reasonably called coals, lighting the nations together and purifying; that these things happened, learn from the things brought next:

choices.english: coals: the chorus of the apostles
choices.why: Pentecost fiery tongues make the apostles coals lighting the nations. Not ‘literal charcoal’.

anf_compare.notes: ANF lacks this Greek catena as reading English.
